passage:
The hostel computer lab was empty at 1 a.m. except for Yamini and the glow of a profile that wasn't hers.
"Anika, 21, loves sunsets and poetry" had a smile Yamini had copied from a stranger's travel photos. Anika had four hundred followers. Yamini, in real life, ate dinner alone most nights.
Lokesh, from the city college, messaged Anika every evening now. Tonight he wrote: "You're the only person I can be real with."
Yamini read it three times. It felt wonderful. It also felt like theft. He was being real with someone who didn't exist, and the girl who did exist was using his trust to feel admired.
He had asked twice for a video call. She had made excuses both times.
She opened a new message and typed, slowly: "There's something true I need to tell you about who I am." Her finger hovered over send.

qa.a: He wrote, "You're the only person I can be real with."

qa.q: Why did the message feel both wonderful and like theft to Yamini?
qa.a: It gave her the admiration she craved, but she knew Lokesh was trusting someone who didn't exist.

qa.q: What should Yamini do while her finger hovers over send?
qa.a: She should send it, tell Lokesh the truth plainly and apologise, and stop using the fake profile, even though it will hurt.

qa.q: How might Lokesh feel when he learns the truth?
qa.a: He may feel shocked, hurt and foolish for sharing so much, even though being deceived is not his fault.

grounding: A lonely student runs a false profile to feel admired, and sees she is using Lokesh's trust whatever her motive.

passage:
Dear Shalini,
For eight months you've known me as Nysa, the singer from Mumbai with the rooftop studio. There is no Nysa. There is no rooftop. I'm Bhavna, nineteen, I live with my parents in Bhopal, and I have never sung in front of anyone.
I made Nysa after a bad year when I felt invisible. The photos were a stranger's. The stories were things I wished were mine. When you started telling me about your exams and your father's illness, I should have stopped. Instead I kept going, because you admired her, and that felt like being admired myself.
Some people make profiles like this to take money, or worse. I didn't, but I still used your trust, and that is wrong whatever my reason.
I'm sorry. I've deleted the account. If you ever want to talk to the real me, I'm here.
Bhavna

qa.a: Bhavna invented Nysa, a singer from Mumbai with a rooftop studio.

qa.q: What did Bhavna feel when Shalini admired Nysa?
qa.a: It felt like being admired personally, which soothed the invisibility Bhavna had felt after a bad year.

qa.q: When should Bhavna have stopped, and what does the letter get right?
qa.a: Bhavna should have stopped when Shalini began sharing real worries; the letter tells the whole truth, deletes the account and admits the trust was used whatever the reason.

qa.q: What might Shalini feel reading this email?
qa.a: Shalini may feel shocked, embarrassed and betrayed after sharing personal things, and may need time before deciding whether to talk.

grounding: Bhavna confesses to inventing a glamorous online persona out of insecurity and admits that Shalini's trust was used regardless of the motive.
